newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended mixed on Thursday after trading in a narrow range at lower levels for most of the day.
Turnover was extremely light, dealers said, with players perplexed as to the direction of the market in the near term.
German and U.S. data through the day had failed to give any clues as to building trends, one said.
"The only direction this afternoon is homewards," he said. "There's nothing going on today, but at these levels we may get some buying tomorrow or on Monday."
Prices in the guilder market were squeezed up a little towards the end of the session, after spending most of the day moving sideways at depressed opening levels.

The Bundesbank's decision to hold German rates unchanged, and the U.S. market's lack of reaction to bond-friendly data there, had some players wary that the debt rally might have run out of steam, a broker said.

Guilders lost ground to bunds in the morning on the spreads, but recovered late in the day. The 10-year yield discount stayed at 13 basis points, while the 30-year discount widened to 23 from 21 on Wednesday.
Some lengthening trades saw the long end of the curve outperforming, traders said, with expected mid-curve action not in evidence yet. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
